an4.170:1.2: On one occasion Ven. Ānanda was staying in Kosambī at Ghosita’s monastery.
an4.170:1.5: “Yes, friend,” the monks responded to him.
an4.170:2.1: “Friends, whoever—monk or nun—declares the attainment of arahantship in my presence, they all do it by means of one or another of four paths.
an4.170:3.2: “There is the case where a monk has developed insight preceded by tranquility.
an4.170:3.3: As he develops insight preceded by tranquility, the path is born.
an4.170:3.4: He follows that path, develops it, pursues it.
an4.170:3.5: As he follows the path, developing it & pursuing it—his fetters are abandoned, his obsessions destroyed.
an4.170:4.1: “Then there is the case where a monk has developed tranquility preceded by insight.
an4.170:4.2: As he develops tranquility preceded by insight, the path is born.
an4.170:4.3: He follows that path, develops it, pursues it.
an4.170:4.4: As he follows the path, developing it & pursuing it—his fetters are abandoned, his obsessions destroyed.
an4.170:5.1: “Then there is the case where a monk has developed tranquility in tandem with insight.
an4.170:5.2: As he develops tranquility in tandem with insight, the path is born.
an4.170:5.3: He follows that path, develops it, pursues it.
an4.170:5.4: As he follows the path, developing it & pursuing it—his fetters are abandoned, his obsessions destroyed.
an4.170:6.1: “Then there is the case where a monk’s mind has its restlessness concerning the Dhamma [Comm: the corruptions of insight] well under control.
an4.170:6.2: There comes a time when his mind grows steady inwardly, settles down, and becomes unified & concentrated.
an4.170:6.3: In him the path is born.
an4.170:6.4: He follows that path, develops it, pursues it.
an4.170:6.5: As he follows the path, developing it & pursuing it—his fetters are abandoned, his obsessions destroyed.
an4.170:7.1: “Whoever—monk or nun—declares the attainment of arahantship in my presence, they all do it by means of one or another of these four paths.”
